title: Health review of Parcel
verdict: Parcel is in fair shape: the domain code is small and well tested. The cost is at its edges: one CI run in seven fails on a browser test that passes when run again, and every change of a shipment field touches five files in three areas. The five changes to make remove about 2,900 lines and the timing waits; none adds a layer.

findings.title: Wait for the map to be ready instead of sleeping
findings.claim: Eleven browser tests sleep 500 ms before reading the map; on CI the map takes up to 1.8 s, so they fail about one run in seven.

evidence.text: 34 of the last 200 runs of `main` failed and passed on the second attempt.
In 29 of these 34, the first attempt failed in a test of `tracking.spec.ts` that passed in the second; the 5 others were cancelled jobs. The table is in `signals/ci-first-attempts.md`.
`await page.waitForTimeout(500)` before the first assertion, in 11 tests.
The map already announces that it is ready, and no test listens.
Reproduced: 7 failures in 40 runs with 2 workers, 0 in 40 with the wait for the attribute, tried in a worktree.

findings.change: Replace the eleven sleeps by one helper that waits for the `data-map-ready` attribute, with the default deadline of the suite. Delete the retry of the CI job once 200 runs are green.

removes: 11 fixed waits (5.5 s of every run)
the `retries: 2` of the CI job, which hides new flaky tests

items.label: wait for `data-map-ready`
items.note: as long as it takes, 10 s at most

findings.firstStep: Add `waitForMap` to `web/tests/helpers.ts` and use it in the first test of `tracking.spec.ts`; run it 40 times with 2 workers.
risks: A test may rely on the sleep for something else than the map: read each assertion that follows.
findings.ifNot: One CI run in seven keeps failing, and the retry keeps hiding the next flaky test.

findings.title: Give each API test its own database file
findings.claim: The API tests share one SQLite file, so they pass or fail with the order in which they run.

evidence.text: One module-level connection for all tests.
3 failures in 10 shuffled runs, 0 in 10 in the default order.

findings.change: Create the database per test from the schema file, in memory. Remove the cleanup code of the tests.

removes: 14 `DELETE FROM` cleanups at the end of tests
adds: one fixture that builds an in-memory database

findings.firstStep: Run the suite shuffled 10 times and keep the list of the tests that fail.
risks: The suite may get slower: measure it before and after.
findings.dissent: The third analyst expects the per-test database to cost about 20 s per run and prefers one transaction per test, rolled back. Not measured yet: the first step decides.

findings.title: Merge the three shipment mappers into the repository
findings.claim: A shipment crosses three mapping layers that each copy every field; adding a field takes five files, and two of the last nine fields were forgotten in one layer.

evidence.text: 31 of the 36 commits that changed `mappers.py` in the last year also changed the four other files.
Fixes for a field lost in a mapper: `a41c9e0`, `77d0b12`.

findings.change: Keep one `Shipment` type. The repository reads and writes it; the two intermediate types and their mappers go away.

removes: the place where a field gets lost

findings.firstStep: Add a test that sends a shipment with every field through the HTTP handler and reads it back.
steps: Delete the tests of the mappers.
verify: The round-trip test passes after each commit.
risks: The public JSON uses `snake_case` names produced by `DtoMapper`: keep them with the serializer settings.
findings.ifNot: Every new field keeps costing five edits and risks the bug seen twice this year.
outOfScope: Do not change the names of the public JSON fields.

findings.title: Delete the unused carrier plug-in interface
findings.claim: `CarrierPlugin` has one implementation since it was added two years ago; callers pay a registry, a factory and a configuration key to reach it.

evidence.text: One class implements it; the registry holds one entry.
No commit added a second carrier since `2024-02`.

findings.change: Call `PostalCarrier` directly. Delete the interface, the registry, the factory and the `carrier.plugin` setting.
findings.firstStep: Replace the two calls of `registry.get("postal")` by `PostalCarrier()`.
verify: The tests of `api/carriers` pass without the registry.
risks: A deployment may set `carrier.plugin`: reading it should fail with a clear message for one release.
findings.ifNot: Small, but every reader of the carrier code pays for it.

findings.title: Rewrite the contributor guide around what a contributor does first
findings.claim: The guide answers "how do I run the tests" on its fourth screen, after the history of the build system; a reader without context needed 2,100 words to find it.

evidence.text: 3,900 words; the commands to build and test start at word 2,100.
Two of its commands no longer exist: `make seed`, `make e2e-fast`.
A reader with only the guide answered 2 of 5 questions correctly.

findings.change: Lead with build, test and submit in one screen. Move the build internals to their own page, linked. Delete the history and the two dead commands.

removes: 2,300 words: history, repeated warnings, dead commands
adds: one linked page for the build internals, moved not written

before.text: Before you begin it is important to understand that, historically, the project used to rely on a set of shell scripts which have since been replaced, although some of them remain for compatibility reasons, and you should therefore be careful, when running the tests, to make sure that you are using the new entry point, which is described further below.

findings.firstStep: Write the five questions the guide must answer; keep the reader test as the check.
verify: A reader with only the guide answers the 5 questions.
Every command of the guide runs.
risks: The history explains two odd choices of the build: keep each as one sentence where the choice is.
